gen-dafont-nordic-gf-stack-sans-headline: Ancient and weighty, Nordic packs its openings tight like a pressed leaf fold. And Stack Sans Headline, a plain sans with wide gaps and a deep middle band, opens everything back up.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-stack-sans-notch: Nordic spaces its letters like brush dabs set far apart, each one cramped shut like a pressed leaf fold. Stack Sans Notch, a plain sans with open curves, is the clear counterweight.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-stack-sans-text: Nordic draws its monoweight strokes with cramped openings, like a pressed leaf fold. Stack Sans Text, a marker-line sans with curve endings kept apart, lets the page breathe around those tight shapes.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-sulphur-point: Sulphur Point keeps its gaps open and its line steady. Nordic is best at looking cramped and ancient, spaced like far-apart brush dabs, while the sans is best at staying open and bulky.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-tiktok-sans: Tight, ancient and powerful, Nordic closes up like a pressed leaf fold. TikTok Sans, a sans-serif with a spacious c and a tall x-height, flings the doors open, which is the pair's whole appeal.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-ubuntu-sans: Ubuntu Sans reads round and tubular, like bent copper pipe. Nordic does best at an ancient, tightly shut, brush-dab look, while the sans does best at big, open lowercase eyes and unfinished curves.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-vend-sans: Vend Sans reads like a ruler-drawn line, with curves left wide and unclosed at the ends. And Nordic, powerful and tightly shut, makes that openness stand out on the page.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-yaldevi: Ancient and powerful, Nordic packs its openings shut in one stroke weight. Yaldevi, a sans with outsized lowercase and an e that opens to the right, gives the eye plenty of room as the lines run on.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-aldrich: Technical and bold, Nulshock stretches wide on spacious tracking. Aldrich, a sans with near-cap x-height and cupped round letters, reads like tracing a single thick thread down the line.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-alexandria: Technical at heart, with letters stretched wide apart. Nulshock does best with a steady outline and no stroke modulation, while Alexandria does best with open c terminals and short stems.
